_doc: Local-kind value-finder for the lazy-checkpoint approach (cardinality cliff). The checkpoint's per-stream fsync/syncfs is not a correctness barrier (ack = WAL fdatasync; recovery replays the retained WAL) — it only bounds WAL size for recycling. So the checkpoint interval is a pure amortization knob: a LARGE interval fires the O(shards) syncfs barrier far less often and coalesces many appends to the same stream into one metadata/journal update, trading a larger retained WAL + longer crash-replay for cheaper steady-state writes. This sweeps the interval (--wal-checkpoint-interval-ms) with syncfs on, against two reference arms (baseline = per-stream fdatasync @3s; syncfs @3s = PR #4697). Local kind is a relative value-finder only (Docker VM fsync != NVMe); if larger intervals lift throughput here, re-tune the actual values on the remote NVMe cluster. Watch WAL_CKPT fsync_us + cadence via --wal-stats 2.
